newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean copper output seen at 3.4 mln tonnes 97.
newsitem.headline: Chilean copper output seen at 3.4 mln tonnes 97.

text.p: Chilean copper output will rise modestly to about 3.39 million tonnes this year from 3.07 million in 1996 as work continues on a new generation of big mining projects, Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky said.
Chile was forecasting an average copper price this year of about $1.00 a lb, Teplizky told a news conference.
"We expect 1997 to be a year of transition, as the projects begun in 1996 and earlier are further developed," he said.
Copper exports this year will reach about $6.8 billion from $5.8 billion this year, he said.
Chile's total mining exports -- including nitrates, silver, molybdenum, gold and a few others -- will rise to $8.05 billion this year from $7.03 billion in 1996, he said.

Teplizky expects total foreign investment in the mining sector to reach about $1 billion this year, plus about $980 million in Chilean government investment in mining, for a total of about $2 billion compared to $1.8 billion last year.
Foreign investment alone stood at $1 billion last year.
Teplizky, outlining the sector's prospects for 1997 and after, said gold output would climb to 56,000 kilos this year from 52,000 kilos in 1996.
Silver production would rise slightly to 1.10 million kilos from 1.09 million kilos, he said.

Overall production in Chile's entire mining sector would grow about nine percent next year, down from about 11 percent in 1996 but "much higher than the 5.5 percent expected for growth in the economy as a whole," he said.
Chilean copper production will rise to 3.8 million tonnes in 1998, 4.4 million in 1999, 4.70 million in 2000, and then hold roughly steady at $4.74 in 2001, figures released by the ministry showed.
